subject: Activate the function of bimodal pattern of activity if the midday temperature is high enough

messages.author: 7b9976a7166ab661
messages.subject: Activate the function of bimodal pattern of activity if the midday temperature is high enough
parts:
Hello, good morning everyone, I hope you are well.
I am writing to ask you how to activate an option in NicheMapR. Let me explain.
 
I think there is a function in NicheMapR to simulate that a diurnal animal can adopt a bimodal pattern of activity if the midday temperature is high enough, but I don't know which it is. I already looked for that function in the NicheMapR github vignettes (GitHub - mrke/NicheMapR: R implementation of Niche Mapper software for biophysical modelling), as well as in the publications of the  package: Kearney & Porter 2017; 2020 Ecography; Kearney 2018 Ecological Monographs; Kearney et al. 2020 Methods in Ecology and Evolution.
Possibly no such function exists, but I think the potential duration of daily activity can be estimated similarly to what was done in Kearney 2013 Ecology Letters.
 
Thank you for your attention.
Regards,
Israel

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Activate the function of bimodal pattern of activity if the midday temperature is high enough
parts:
Hi Israel,

The bimodal activity just emerges from what you set the body temperature thresholds for activity to, and from what the microclimate is like. If it's getting too hot in the shade, or if you didn't allow them any, the model will put them in their retreat underground by default. Does that make sense?

All the best,
Mike
